translation: The arm bone (臂骨): from the elbow to the wrist there are two roots, the principal and the auxiliary. The one below, which is long and large in form and connects to the tip of the elbow, is the arm bone (臂骨); the one above, which is short and thin in form, is the auxiliary bone (輔骨), commonly called the chan bone (纏骨). They lie stacked and leaning against each other, and both connect below to the wrist bone (腕骨). In all cases where the arm bone is injured, it is mostly broken by a blow received head-on.
